subject: Throughput collapse from burst-window mismatch — Brightline production
messages:
From: Rajesh Kumar <r.kumar@brightline.health>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: platform@brightline.health
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden surge in 429s and end-to-end latency — Brightline prod

Hi Soojin,

We're seeing a sharp increase in 429 responses and 2-3x p95 generation latency across our most critical route (POST /v1/generate). Traffic volume hasn't increased on our side — last deploy was yesterday morning. This started ~08:40 PT. Throughput to your API seems capped; requests are being throttled after a short burst.

Quick summary:
- Region: us-west-2
- Impact: ~15% of requests 429, another 25% with >2s latency spikes
- Affects: production route tied to model redwood-std-32k

Can you confirm if any rate-limiting or burst policy changes were rolled out? We need an immediate mitigation path — even a temporary increase in burst allowance or routing to alternate capacity would help.

Attaching a small sample of our client-side logs.

Thanks,
Rajesh
Platform Engineer — Brightline Health

Attachment: client_request_sample.log (text/plain)

- Naomi: I’ll coordinate maintenance window and customer comms.

— Soojin

So: +1 415-555-0192

From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
To: soojin.lee@redwood.ai, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:41:37 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden surge in 429s and end-to-end latency — Brightline prod

Initial findings (quick scan of control-plane logs and token-bucket metrics):
- We pushed a policy refactor to routing rules at 08:15 PT to support per-customer routing weights. The refactor introduced a new burst_window default of 2s for routes without an explicit override.
- Brightline's production route relied on the previous implicit burst_window (~8s) to absorb short traffic spikes. With the new default, the token-bucket drains quickly and triggers 429s.
- Additionally, the per-route quota check is being applied before cross-customer capacity pooling due to ordering changes in the policy engine — requests are not seeing fallback capacity.

Immediate mitigations I can apply now (estimate 10-15m):
1) Increase route burst_window to 10s for brightline-prod (hot patch).
2) Temporarily disable the new ordering so capacity pooling occurs before per-route quotas for affected customers.
3) Route a subset of Brightline traffic to a spare dedicated pool (if accepted).

I’m attaching a concise diagnostic excerpt and the diff for the policy change. I'll apply 1) and 2) now and monitor.

Attachment: diagnostic_log_excerpt.txt (text/plain)
Attachment: rate_policy_diff.patch (text/x-patch)

- Marcus
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@brightline.health>, Rajesh Kumar <r.kumar@brightline.health>, soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:58:05 -07:00
Subject: Service update and proposed maintenance window — Brightline production

Hi Lena / Rajesh,

Thank you for reporting this — Marcus has identified a configuration regression that reduced the burst window for unrouted routes. Marcus will apply an emergency hotfix now (increase burst_window) and revert the ordering regression so fallback pooling is used. We expect visible improvement within ~15 minutes.

Proposed short maintenance window for a safer rollback: Today 10:15–10:30 PT (15 minutes). During that time we may route a subset of traffic to alternate capacity; there should be a short blip but no sustained downtime.

We’ll also follow up with a post-incident write-up and a proposed credit for impacted requests. Can you confirm the 10:15 window?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@brightline.health>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: Rajesh Kumar <r.kumar@brightline.health>, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:03:21 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service update and proposed maintenance window — Brightline production

Thanks Naomi — 10:15 PT works. We appreciate the quick response.

Two asks from Brightline leadership:
- Please confirm what percentage of our traffic will be impacted by the routing step during the window.
- We will expect compensation for the degraded user experience (recommendation: credits + SLA exception for this period).

We’re switching one of our workflows to a backup model, but we'd like to avoid repeated hits to production if the rollback isn't complete. Looping in Rajesh for details.

— Lena
Head of Platform, Brightline Health

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec summary and next steps — Brightline incident (burst-window misalignment)

Team — quick exec note to capture decisions and asks for follow-up:

What happened:
- A policy refactor introduced a shortened default burst_window and changed quota ordering. Brightline's production route relied on the previous behavior and experienced throttling and elevated latency as a result.

Immediate actions taken:
- Marcus applied hotfixes: increased burst_window to 10s for brightline-prod and reverted ordering so capacity pooling occurs before per-route quotas. Visible 429 reduction within 12 minutes.
- Naomi coordinated a 15-minute window (10:15 PT) to stabilize routing; Brightline confirmed.
- Sales committed to a credit proposal: 10% invoice credit for the impacted billing period; AE to confirm details with customer.

Open items / next steps (owners):
- Postmortem (Marissa) — include timeline, root cause, and remediation plan (deadline: 2027-05-27).
- Policy guardrails (Marcus) — add automated tests and CI gating for default burst_window changes; review policy ordering semantics (deadline: 2027-05-30).
- Customer comms & credits (Soojin + Naomi) — final credit amount and legal review (deadline: 2027-05-24).
- Monitoring & Alerts (SRE) — add an alert for rapid change in token-bucket drain rate and for sudden p95 jumps tied to quota enforcement (deadline: 2027-05-25).

Please update the JIRA ticket JIRA-RDWD-1298 with progress and attach the postmortem draft. We should also prepare a short external-safe summary for Brightline.

— Lauren
VP Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: postmortem_draft.md (text/markdown)
